name: Siege
overview: Scripture provides clear instructions regarding the conduct of a siege, emphasizing that an offer of peace must be extended to a city before engaging in warfare against it, as stated in Deuteronomy 20:10-11. If the city refuses peace and chooses to fight, a siege is then to be conducted, involving the construction of bulwarks and careful management of resources, including the preservation of fruit-bearing trees during the siege (Deuteronomy 20:12, 19-20). The historical record, such as the capture of Jerusalem by the sons of Judah (Judges 1:8), illustrates the serious and often devastating nature of sieges in biblical times.
